label: Case Study Rail
description: Process-led portfolio that presents work as horizontal case studies: problem, approach, result. For studios that sell a method, not a moodboard.
signatureMotif: horizontal case rails with problem, process, and a hard result
promptHints: Index is a stack of case rails: name, sector, one result number, and a still. Clicking opens a process story, not a lightbox of pretty shots.
Each case uses the same spine: Context → Approach → Outcome. Imagery supports the steps.
Keep type calm. This is a consulting/studio method page, not a loud showcase wall.

layouts: Home lists 4–7 cases as full-width rails (min-h-40): left text (client, year, one-line problem), right a single still, and a result numeral at the far edge.
Case page is a vertical process: a short brief, 3 numbered approach blocks with one image each, then a result band with a metric and a quote. No masonry gallery as the first screen.
About sits after work and states the method in 4–6 lines plus a contact CTA — not a giant personal hero.
Navigation is Work / Method / Contact. Avoid a visual-only grid of thumbnails without captions.
motifs: Off-white ground, near-black type, one muted rust or slate accent for numerals (01, 02, 03).
Instrument Serif for case titles; Inter for process body. Wide tracking on sector labels.
Photos are workplace or product-in-use, captioned. No decorative grain overlays.
antiPatterns: Do not use showcase-bold: oversized full-bleed hero, screaming type, or a thumbnail wall without process.
Avoid minimal-studio empty pages that are only whitespace and a name — this variant must show method.
No 3-up pretty project cards with hover zoom and no problem/result text.
